calls.title: RazorPay & Growthbook Pricing
calls.summary: The team is exploring the pros and cons of building an internal experimentation platform versus partnering for Magic Checkout. Anurag Allamsetty emphasized the need for clearer financial comparisons, while James Shannon highlighted that the estimated enterprise build cost exceeds $300,000 USD, prompting discussions on a lower entry price with success-based pricing models. Experimentation is seen as essential for improving merchant conversion rates, which can lead to increased revenue via reduced churn. Attribution challenges arise in isolating the effects of experimentation on retention; therefore, both parties have agreed to explore metrics linked to retention uplift among active experimenters. Next steps include sharing lifetime value data to refine the pricing model ahead of a planned rollout by early May.
calls.keywords: Experimentation platform, Pricing model, Retention uplift, Build vs. buy decision, Tiered licensing fees, Merchant conversion

calls.title: Razorpay & Growthbook Technical Discussion
calls.summary: The team evaluated the options of building an in-house A/B testing platform or purchasing Growth Book’s solution. Anurag confirmed that building is feasible within three to four weeks, targeting a rollout by the end of April to fulfill commitments to top merchants. Commercial factors are secondary to capability and scale. Growth Book's pricing is significantly higher than competitors like Statsig, raising concerns about budget. A POC will be defined and kicked off within a week, and both parties agreed to collaborate on a cost-benefit analysis to assist the decision-making process.
calls.keywords: Build-vs-Buy, Experimentation Platform, Pricing Model, Self-hosted Deployment, AB Testing, Statistical Analysis
